reuse.why: Extends the existing getDateWithSkippedWeekend and reuses recurConfigToRSchedule, but app.ts writes its own isHoliday instead of exporting the new isSkippedDay, and the daily-skip decision is re-derived at each consumer.

duplication.why: Holiday matching exists twice (isSkippedDay in shared/schedules.ts and isHoliday in server/schedules/app.ts), and the 'daily + skipWeekend -> drop weekend/holiday occurrences, else move' dispatch with its over-fetch heuristic is written three times (getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange).

placement.why: The move-to-nearest-allowed-day rule correctly lives in shared/schedules.ts, but the skip rule and holiday matching are spread into server/schedules/app.ts handlers instead of staying beside it.

scope.why: Changes stay on schedule date computation, types and tests, though getUpcomingDates is reworked (dedupe, over-fetch) beyond what the steps strictly require.

maintainability.why: A future change to which days are skipped must be made in several hand-synchronised places, the over-fetch counts (holidays.length + 7/8) are ad hoc, and schedule-template.ts still calls getDateWithSkippedWeekend without holidays or the daily-skip rule.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/schedules/app.ts isHoliday reimplements the holiday test of isSkippedDay; server/budget/schedule-template.ts keeps calling getDateWithSkippedWeekend without holidays and without the daily skip.

disguised_duplication.where: isHoliday (app.ts) is isSkippedDay minus the weekend test under another name; the daily-skip dispatch is reshaped as filter-then-map in getUpcomingDates, map-to-null-then-filter in getDatesInRange and take/filter/slice in getNextDate.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains a holidays parameter (its loop generalises cleanly); getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange re-implement the daily-skip and holiday checks around it, and schedule-template.ts runSchedule calls it without holidays.
